messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Anomaly detected during canary rollforward to model v5.3 on /v1/chat/stream. p99 spike + intermittent stream stalls. Thread root ts: 2965432100

Irene: saw the alert. I'm taking lead. Quick read: p95 jumped ~150ms -> 430ms, p99 ~5s for streaming chunk gaps. Some streams are stalling where no chunk is emitted for >3s.

Ryan: checking infra metrics now. Router queue depth up on canary routing shard. Encoder host GPU util ~97%, memcpy latency per token increased significantly. Network looks fine.

Maria: SLO alarm fired for streaming-slo.prod (p99 < 2s). We should immediately stop pushing more canary traffic. Any 5xxs? Not seeing 5xxs but many long tails. Customer impact unknown yet.

Irene: mitigation plan (short): 1) pause rollforward 2) shift streaming route away from canary to stable 3) rollback if p99 not restored within 10m. Executing: /deploy-bot halt-rollforward --canary v5.3

deploy-bot: Accepted. Halting rollforward for v5.3. Reverting traffic policy to keep 100% of new sessions on v5.2. Existing sessions will drain (max 60s).

Neil: pulling encoder logs. Seeing repeated KV cache misses and heavy CPU<->GPU memcopies under multi-context requests. v5.3 seems to increase ephemeral KV churn.

Irene: can someone run quick kv cache query? e.g.:
```
select avg(kv_cache_miss_rate), p95(memcpy_ms) from encoder_metrics where model="v5.3" group by shard
```

Ryan: results: kv_cache_miss_rate ~0.45 on canary shards vs ~0.06 on stable; memcpy p95 from 1.0ms -> 3.8ms. Matches GPU transfer pressure theory.

Maria: customer-impact calc: affected ~7.8% of streaming sessions globally; ~0.7% had stall >5s. No immediate billing-impact but CS should prepare outreach for any high-touch customers.

prod-manager: tagging customers in east-1 with long-lived sessions. @cs-team prepare targeted messages.

sre-lead: live actions: keep rollforward halted, route traffic off canary, if p99 not under SLO within 10m then rollback canary and preserve instances for RCA. Capture perf traces & heap snapshots.

Irene: initiating rollback: /deploy-bot rollback-canary --target v5.2 --reason "encoder KV thrash causing p99 spike"

deploy-bot: Rollback started. Swap expected ~90s. New sessions will target v5.2 post-swap.

eng-oncall: PR 4872 is the recent encoder refactor (buffer reuse + tokenization change). Will pull the diff and run local reproducer.

Ryan: monitoring after rollback trigger: p95 trending down to ~160ms, p99 dropping under 1.9s. One shard (shard-7a) shows residual tailing. Suggest isolating that host and draining.

Neil: collecting GPU perf dumps and core logs from shard-7a. Uploads to /incidents/2965432100/artifacts.

Irene: observation: kv_cache_miss hotspot correlates with cross-chunk token alignments introduced by v5.3 tokenizer tweak. eng-oncall, can you validate whether buffer reuse path triggers extra allocations when alignment != 0?

eng-oncall: reproducer confirms: when prompt chunk alignments cross certain boundaries, the optimizer path bypasses reuse and allocates temporary KV slices. Fix candidate: force reuse path or collapse allocations for crossed-align cases. Preparing a PR.

Maria: drafting short incident summary for CS: root cause hypothesis, affected endpoints, percent affected, mitigation steps taken, next steps and ETA for RCA. Will share in 12m for review.

prod-manager: CS notified targeted customers. No escalations yet. If impact persists >30m, we'll post brief status update.

sre-lead: keep the canary instances up (do not terminate) for postmortem traces. Assignments: Irene (incident lead), Neil (metrics & artifacts), eng-oncall (repro + fix), Maria (customer comms).

Irene: watch window active. Rollback completed at 2965432300, p99 below SLO overall. Draining and scaling down shard-7a now. Watch until 2965434200 (~1 hour). Handoff to @Ryan in 15m. React with :thumbsup: when you read.

Ryan: :thumbsup: I'll take watch. If p99 > 2.0s again, I'll re-escalate pager and coordinate a scale/rollback.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: Irene -> Ryan at 2965432540. Watch window active until 2965434200.
